title: Does AI trading actually make people serious money, or is this mostly hype?
author: gokubalck_69
selftext:
I keep seeing posts/ads about "AI trading bots" making people consistent profits, and I genuinely can't tell how much of it is real vs marketing.

Some things I'm trying to understand:

Are there legit, verifiable cases of individual traders using AI/algo strategies to make significant, consistent returns not backtested screenshots, but real audited track records?

How much of "AI trading" success is actually just standard quant/algo trading (which has existed for decades) getting rebranded with an AI label?

For people who've actually built or used trading bots/models What are the actual failure modes people don't talk about overfitting to backtests, execution costs, slippage, models breaking in new market regimes?

Not looking for signals or bot recommendations genuinely trying to separate real experience from the marketing noise. If you've actually run one live (not backtested) I'd love to hear how it really went, good or bad.

comments.author: mdawe1
comments.body: AI for research and programming...yes. Hard AI in your work flow for strict Day Trading.... not that I have seen. I have tried various approaches and non provided  alpha just extra ops costs. Maybe if you trained your own local AI box but I haven't tried that yet. AI are super risk adverse and getting them to be bullish with live money is a trick onto its self

replies.author: siem
replies.body: Any pointers on how to get AI bullish?

replies.author: joshman1204
replies.body: Give it structured targets. For example one of my agents is given instructions for using atr to calculate stop placements and then forced into a minimum R:R. If a trade passes these gates the llm is forced to evaluate it and it can only choose not to trade if it has a concrete invalidation reason with evidence.

replies.author: mdawe1
replies.body:
I also put firewalls between the AI doing a scoring mechanism (catalyst interpetation or whatever) and the Bot that buys if the score is xxx or more... stuff like that. The min it knows its live money it goes weak.  
Also AI has no consistent intelligence level. It varies heavily by development cycle and even time of day.

replies.author: joshman1204
replies.body: You hit one of the hardest things nobody expects. The "smarter" the model the more risk adverse it becomes. I think this is driven by the AI's internal assistant mentality and how small the chances of a trade actually being profitable truly are. The ai knows losing money is bad and not helpful so it just chooses to write a really convincing narrative about any small reason it can find to avoid trading.

replies.author: mdawe1
replies.body: I have also seen this get into back-testing results. I have seen it assume crazy high slippage to justify not promoting a set of params.

comments.author: silphotographer
comments.body:
That's like saying do cars make you more productive with life? Depends. 

Generally speaking AI cannot be depended to make trading judgement because it cannot rationalize and reason it is the most sophisticated fill in the blank large language model but you may not like what it autofills. 

IMHO LLM (because that's what it really is not a true AGI) is best used to automate exhaustively laborious task where processing power and computation is most needed not reasoning or judgement decision making process. Under competent hands where an expert knows what to do but just lack the time/energy/labor LLM can be a powerful tool. For someone who doesn't know shit and wanna compensate by overly depending on LLM is gonna have a bad time.

comments.author: joshman1204
comments.body:
I'm almost $35k deep into my agentic trading build. Anyone saying they are making serious money with AI agents trading is likely either lying or just got lucky.

I still believe it is an achievable goal but it is orders of magnitude harder than most people expect it to be.

This month is the first month the trading has been profitable. My agents have been trading real money via an ibkr account for 3 months now. July I made about $200 income from the trading agent on a roughly $10k account. However I spent $1k in ai subscriptions and API fees for agentic inference via deepseek. So all in still a loss this month but atleast the agent had a positive pnl for the first time.

replies.author: joshman1204
replies.body: It's not all subscriptions. I have Claude max, codex pro or whatever it's called, and then the rest is either deepseek API that the agents actually use or random stuff like Voyage ai for embeddings or grok for random x related stuff. So maybe $450 or so is subscriptions everything else is API for various services.

comments.author: gokubalck_69
comments.body: You surely  have guts to spend 35k in this

comments.author: TacticalDataDesk
comments.body:
Yes it works. I have four AI driven automated trading systems. 1. CVD Divergence, 2. Fibonacci Trader, 3. Market Structure, and 4. Project Judas. 

  
CVD Divergence has $6,000 profit between ES and NQ today

Fibonacci Trader has is even (wins on ES and MNQ, loss on GC and NQ)

Market Structure is $1,500 (+$1,500 on NQ, -$500 on ES, +$450 on GC). Earlier NQ was up $4,000.

Project Judas is up $5,500 between GC, SIL, MNQ, NQ, and ES.

  
So yes they work. Yes they are a lot of work, and yes you need to refine your model to be efficient and effective through any market. Not just up trends, down trends, or flat periods. It must be trained. 

  
It is not as simple as saying "Hey Claude, make me some money."

replies.body: Can you elaborate what ES MNQ GC NQ SIL are?

replies.body: Not to be that guy but this is exactly the kind of bullshit that needs to be pointed out. This account is clearly just trying to get clicks to a website and sell you a course or some bs subscription.

comments.author: johnfkngzoidberg
comments.body: Ai is great for research and automating the dumb stuff.  It’s terrible for making actual financial decisions because it’s mostly a sycophant toddler with no common sense.  My bot grabs research, narrows down stuff, does the monkey work, then I look at what’s left and trade.

comments.author: papapumpnz
comments.body:
Nope its all bullshit. Nobodys making money. Any demos you see of amazing results are all bullshit, either completely fabricated to sell a platform so the devs make money from you, its all backtest smoke and mirrors and wouldn't make money live, or they make a profit in tiny slices, but you only see the tiny slice, not the huge losses outside of it.

So I think not.
